plain_explanation: A model predicts likely next pieces of text. The surrounding application chooses evidence, enforces access, and checks the result. A manual answer sheet gives a baseline. A replayed response is useful for an outage but cannot measure fresh model variability.
worked_example: Of ten policy questions, seven answers are supported, two are wrong and one should have abstained. Supported task accuracy is 7/10 = 70%. Repeating two recorded prompts gives two different wordings, but both may be correct. Compare meaning and evidence rather than exact spelling.

exam.question: Explain generation versus prediction with one example of each.
exam.model_answer: Predict whether an email is spam: a label. Generate a reply: new text. Both use learned patterns and both can be wrong.

exam.question: Seven of ten answers are correct and supported. Calculate accuracy and name a missing check.
exam.model_answer: 7/10 = 70%. Also check permissions, unsupported claims or repeated-run variation.

exam.question: Why can a fluent answer be wrong?
exam.model_answer: Likely wording is not proof of a claim. Compare the statement with the source or reference answer.
